325: /// This is our bridge between tokio-rustls and hyper. It implements
326: /// `hyper::server::accept::Accept` interface, producing TLS-over-TCP
327: /// connections.
328: ///
329: /// Internally, it creates a stream that produces fully negotiated TLS
330: /// connections as they come in from a TCP listen socket.  This stream allows
331: /// for multiple TLS connections to be negotiated concurrently with new
332: /// connections being accepted.
333: struct HttpsAcceptor {
334:     stream: Box<dyn Stream<Item = std::io::Result<TlsConn>> + Send + Unpin>,
335: }
336: 
337: impl HttpsAcceptor {
338:     pub fn new(
339:         log: slog::Logger,
340:         tls_acceptor: Arc<Mutex<TlsAcceptor>>,
341:         tcp_listener: TcpListener,
342:     ) -> HttpsAcceptor {
343:         HttpsAcceptor {
344:             stream: Box::new(Box::pin(Self::new_stream(
345:                 log,
346:                 tls_acceptor,
347:                 tcp_listener,
348:             ))),
349:         }
350:     }
351: 
352:     fn new_stream(
353:         log: slog::Logger,
354:         tls_acceptor: Arc<Mutex<TlsAcceptor>>,
355:         tcp_listener: TcpListener,
356:     ) -> impl Stream<Item = std::io::Result<TlsConn>> {
357:         stream! {
358:             let mut tls_negotiations = futures::stream::FuturesUnordered::new();
359:             loop {
360:                 tokio::select! {
361:                     Some(negotiation) = tls_negotiations.next(), if
362:                             !tls_negotiations.is_empty() => {
363: 
364:                         match negotiation {
365:                             Ok(conn) => yield Ok(conn),
366:                             Err(e) => {
367:                                 // If TLS negotiation fails, log the cause but
368:                                 // don't forward it along. Yielding an error
369:                                 // from here will terminate the server.
370:                                 // These failures may be a fatal TLS alert
371:                                 // message, or a client disconnection during
372:                                 // negotiation, or other issues.
373:                                 // TODO: We may want to export a counter for
374:                                 // different error types, since this may contain
375:                                 // useful things like "your certificate is
376:                                 // invalid"
377:                                 warn!(log, "tls accept err: {}", e);
378:                             },
379:                         }
380:                     },
381:                     accept_result = tcp_listener.accept() => {
382:                         let (socket, addr) = match accept_result {
383:                             Ok(v) => v,
384:                             Err(e) => {
385:                                 match e.kind() {
386:                                     std::io::ErrorKind::ConnectionAborted => {
387:                                         continue;
388:                                     },
389:                                     // The other errors that can be returned
390:                                     // under POSIX are all programming errors or
391:                                     // resource exhaustion. For now, handle
392:                                     // these by no longer accepting new
393:                                     // connections.
394:                                     // TODO-robustness: Consider handling these
395:                                     // more gracefully.
396:                                     _ => {
397:                                         yield Err(e);
398:                                         break;
399:                                     }
400:                                 }
401:                             }
402:                         };
403: 
404:                         let tls_negotiation = tls_acceptor
405:                             .lock()
406:                             .await
407:                             .accept(socket)
408:                             .map_ok(move |stream| TlsConn::new(stream, addr));
409:                         tls_negotiations.push(tls_negotiation);
410:                     },
411:                     else => break,
412:                 }
413:             }
414:         }
415:     }
416: }

169: // it binds to ports as expected.
170: async fn test_config_bind_server<C, T>(test_config: T, bind_port: u16)
171: where
172:     C: hyper::client::connect::Connect + Clone + Send + Sync + 'static,
173:     T: TestConfigBindServer<C>,
174: {
175:     let client = test_config.make_client();
176: 
177:     // Make sure there is not currently a server running on our expected
178:     // port so that when we subsequently create a server and run it we know
179:     // we're getting the one we configured.
180:     let error = client.get(test_config.make_uri(bind_port)).await.unwrap_err();
181:     assert!(error.is_connect());
182: 
183:     // Now start a server with our configuration and make the request again.
184:     // This should succeed in terms of making the request.  (The request
185:     // itself might fail with a 400-level or 500-level response code -- we
186:     // don't want to depend on too much from the ApiServer here -- but we
187:     // should have successfully made the request.)
188:     let server = test_config.make_server(bind_port);
189:     client.get(test_config.make_uri(bind_port)).await.unwrap();
190:     server.close().await.unwrap();
191: 
192:     // Make another request to make sure it fails now that we've shut down
193:     // the server.  We need a new client to make sure our client-side connection
194:     // starts from a clean slate.  (Otherwise, a race during shutdown could
195:     // cause us to successfully send a request packet, only to have the TCP
196:     // stack return with ECONNRESET, which gets in the way of what we're trying
197:     // to test here.)
198:     let client = test_config.make_client();
199:     let error = client.get(test_config.make_uri(bind_port)).await.unwrap_err();
200:     assert!(error.is_connect());
201: 
202:     // Start a server on another TCP port and make sure we can reach that
203:     // one (and NOT the one we just shut down).
204:     let server = test_config.make_server(bind_port + 1);
205:     client.get(test_config.make_uri(bind_port + 1)).await.unwrap();
206:     let error = client.get(test_config.make_uri(bind_port)).await.unwrap_err();
207:     assert!(error.is_connect());

212:     let error =
213:         client.get(test_config.make_uri(bind_port + 1)).await.unwrap_err();
